titlePlain: A Portable Workload Deployed Identically to
subtitle: Lesson 30 · Capstone: Designing a Hybrid/Multi-Cloud Architecture

eyebrow: Reusing the Chapter 3 module, not rewriting it
caption: Same module source, called twice -- only the inputs each cloud genuinely requires differ.

code:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: claims-burst-worker
spec:
  replicas: 3
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: claims-burst-worker
          image: registry.alderney.example/claims-burst-worker:2.3.0

# kubectl --context aks-alderney apply -f claims-burst-worker.yaml
# kubectl --context eks-alderney apply -f claims-burst-worker.yaml
caption: Same file, same kubectl apply, two different clusters.

steps.label: Portable core stays in one file
steps.sub: Only the genuinely cloud-specific value lives in two small files

code:
kubectl --context aks-alderney get deployment claims-burst-worker -o wide
kubectl --context eks-alderney get deployment claims-burst-worker -o wide

kubectl --context aks-alderney exec deploy/claims-burst-worker -- curl -s localhost:8080/healthz
kubectl --context eks-alderney exec deploy/claims-burst-worker -- curl -s localhost:8080/healthz
caption: Same replica count, same ready status, same healthz response on both clusters.
